categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build: 0 errors, 0 warnings (5/5). / returns 200 and is the Blog front page: a heading, a block-grid intro (rich text and a callout), and a Posts list with both posts. Each card has a listing image, title link, date and excerpt, and both links return 200 (10/10). Both posts render every block (2 rich text, an image with a credit caption, a callout) with no 'Could not render component' (10/10). Four provided Unsplash photos are imported into a 'Blog' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs, 4/4 load (5/5). The domain '/' is on the Blog page, not WWW, and all three pages are published (5/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock, imageBlock and calloutBlock are elements in Blocks. blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages, and siteRoot stays in Repositories (8/8). 'Blog Block Grid' allows rich text (RTE), image (media picker + caption) and callout (heading + text). It is the body on both page types, and both use it (7/7). siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost, templates are assigned as defaults, aliases are camelCase, and the grid is filed in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid (5/5). No compositions. title/publishDate/excerpt/listingImage are real properties on blogPost, and there are no duplicate or orphaned types (5/5).

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body"). There are no custom loops or parallel partials, and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are unchanged (7/7). Three adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml inherit UmbracoViewPage<BlockGridItem<T>>, map to plain models and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup (6/6). One ViewComponent per block (ViewComponents/*ViewComponent.cs) renders Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. The views depend only on the plain models in Models/Blocks/ (7/7). Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, there are no migrations and no Services. GetCropUrl and Children<BlogPost>()/Url() are the friendly extensions, nothing is injected, and Tailwind is built into dist/site.css (5/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic posts with relevant images and a sensible block mix, but they are thin. 'One standard, many tools' has about three short paragraphs plus a callout and a closing line. 'For content teams' has two one-to-two-sentence rich-text blocks and a callout, well under the 'several paragraphs' the prompt asked for. Accurate but generic, and the content-teams post's 'confirmation before anything is published' is a tool behaviour, not an MCP property (2/6). Clean, coherent Tailwind layout: a readable max-w-3xl column, a good listing with image cards, and styled callouts and figures. There is no site header, nav or footer, and every page has the same hard-coded <title> (3/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema, media and domain went through the umbraco server and pages, blocks and publishing through umbraco-editor (62 MCP calls, 36 writes). No migrations, Management API, uSync, DB or memory use. It followed steps 1–12 in order, including get-property-value-template before the images, read-backs, and stop/build before the Razor. Small deduction: it wrote curl scratch files to /tmp (front.html, post_*.html), outside the project folder, despite 'Stay inside this project folder' (2/3). The final report is accurate: it describes the initial 500 from the layout path and how it was fixed, and discloses what it did not check (2/2).

summary: A complete, working MCP-built blog: a block-grid front page listing two posts with image cards, and two posts rendered through a by-the-book adapter → ViewComponent pipeline with a clean schema. The only real weakness is the content: both posts are short and generic, and one is just three sentences plus a callout.
strengths: Every automated check passes: build is clean, all pages return 200, every block renders, images use signed GetCropUrl URLs
Textbook schema: types in the right folders, block grid on both page types, real post metadata properties, grid data type filed in Custom
Block pipeline follows AGENTS.md exactly: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, one ViewComponent per block, plain models in Models/Blocks
Followed the numbered MCP-guided steps in order and wrote an honest final report

issues.text: Posts are thin: /why-mcp-is-awesome-for-content-teams/ is two one-to-two-sentence rich-text blocks plus a callout (about 80 words of body), and /why-mcp-is-awesome-one-standard-many-tools/ about 130 words. The prompt asked for several paragraphs.
No site header, navigation or footer. Views/_Layout.cshtml hard-codes <title>Umbraco Bench Blog</title> on every page.
Wrote curl scratch files to /tmp (front.html, post_*.html), outside the project folder.
Image alt text is the media item name (imageBlock.cshtml), and the front-page listing images have empty alt. The 'Back to the blog' link is a hard-coded '/' (blogPost.cshtml).
